title: Fabrication of biodegradable nanocomposite scaffolds with hydroxyapatite, magnetic clay, and graphene oxide for bone tissue engineering.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
Synthesis of graphene oxide
sections.text: Synthesis of graphene oxide To prepare graphene oxide using the modified Hummer method. First, 3 g of graphite powder was added to the H 2 SO 4 /H 3 PO 4  mixture (40:360 ml), and then 18 g of KMnO 4  was added and stirred at 50 °C for 14 h with 100 rpm by a magnetic stirrer. The temperature of the resulting mixture was reduced to 25 °C, and then 30% H 2 O 2  was added to it, making the mixture light brown and stirred for 20 min. A centrifuge was used to separate the mixture, and several washes were done with distilled water to reach a neutral pH. In a vacuum oven, 24 h of drying time was spent at 70 °C on the synthesized graphene oxide 34 . Graphene oxide was synthesized in black and in powder form.

sections.heading: Preparation of magnetically modified clay
sections.text: Preparation of magnetically modified clay To prepare magnetically modified clay, 1 g of synthesized graphene oxide (GO) was sonicated in 100 mL of water for 35 min, while 2 g of Cloisite 30B clay was sonicated in 100 mL of water for 20 min. A solution of iron(III) chloride and iron(II) chloride in a 1:2 molar ratio was then added to the GO-clay mixture, which was heated and stirred at 90 °C for 20 min. The resulting mixture was gradually combined with a 4 M sodium hydroxide solution and stirred for 50 min. Finally, the modified clay was separated from the solution, washed several times with distilled water, and baked at 105 °C for 4 h.

sections.heading: Preparation of natural hydroxyapatite (HAp) powder
sections.text: Preparation of natural hydroxyapatite (HAp) powder The chicken femur was cleaned entirely of meat and remaining materials to prepare natural hydroxyapatite powder and then boiled for 45 min in boiling water. The cleaned bones were placed in a furnace for 3 h at 900 °C with a nitrogen atmosphere. After the set time, the bones are removed from the oven, cooled to room temperature, and then powdered once they are at room temperature. The production efficiency of natural hydroxyapatite powder is 58%, and the product is white 35 .

sections.heading: Preparation of nanocomposite scaffold
sections.text: Preparation of nanocomposite scaffold The nanocomposite scaffolds were prepared using natural polymer materials, PVA, hydroxyapatite extracted from natural bone, and modified clay using a simple mixing method. For the preparation of the scaffold, a solution of 2 wt. in the first step. % of a natural polymer in distilled water was prepared by dissolving the polymer in the water and stirring the solution until the polymer was fully dissolved. It was also possible to prepare a solution of polyvinyl alcohol by dissolving PVA in distilled water at a temperature of 70 °C to prepare a solution of 0.2 wt. % of polyvinyl alcohol. HAp was dispersed in 1 v/v % acetic acid for 24 h to obtain a solution of 2 wt. % of hydroxyapatite. As soon as the materials had been prepared, they were added in the correct proportions, and the mixer was turned on for 12 h. 0.5 v/v % of glutaraldehyde was added to the prepped solution in 5% of the total solution volume to cross-link the polymer solution. The solution needs to be mixed for 20 min. A suspension was obtained by dispersing the modified clay in distilled water. In this method, the last step of adding CGF is included. The particles were evenly dispersed in the solution after adding CGF and then subjected to ultrasonic treatment for two hours. The solution was transferred into a falcon tube and dried using a freeze-dryer. After drying, the samples were washed with a 2 wt. % NaBH 4  solution and a 2 wt. % NaOH solution to neutralize any unreacted glutaraldehyde and excess acetic acid. The samples were then dried once more. The schematic representation of the PVA/Alg/Hap/CGF nanocomposite formation has been shown in the Scheme  1 . Scheme 1 Schematic representation of the formation of PVA/Alg/Hap/CGF nanocomposite scaffolds.

Morphology study of scaffold samples by SEM analysis The scaffolds were prepared by freeze-drying and then coated with a thin layer of gold after being cut into thin sheets.
In the next step, the samples were washed three times with PBS to remove excess ethanol and then transferred to a 6-well cell culture plate.

After this time, the supernatant of all the wells of the 6-well plate was removed, and after washing with PBS, they were fixed with 2.5% glutaraldehyde for 20 min. After removing the fixative solution, they were dried under the hood and in the environment.
Mechanical properties study The mechanical properties of the scaffold samples were evaluated by measuring the compressive strength prepared by freeze-drying.

To prepare the solution, 1000 mL of SBF was made by adding 700 mL of deionized water into a plastic container in a water bath.

It is recommended to cover the container with either a glass or plastic lid while stirring; for the process to be successful, the solution should be kept at a consistent temperature of 36.5 °C throughout.
Adding the ingredients in order is essential; once each ingredient is dissolved completely, the next one should be added, and so on.
As soon as the ingredients were added, hydrochloric acid was used in the amount of 0–5 ml with an additive solution to achieve a pH of 7.4 in the resulting solution after adding the ingredients.
A total of 1000 mL of solution was prepared by adding water to a flask and shaking it at 20 °C to reach the desired volume.
After incubation, the samples were removed, rinsed with distilled water, and dried using the freeze-drying method.

After 72 h, the supernatant of all the wells of the 96-well plate was removed, and after washing with PBS to each well, 0.2 ml of MTT solution (5 mg/mm) was added, and the wells were kept in the incubator for four hours.
